utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are two judges this afternoon. Judge Picard is unable to continue to hear that case for the remainder of this day, and Judge Gwaunza and myself have considered whether it would be in the interests of justice to continue to hear that case and we have come to the conclusion that it is. We, therefore, will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please be seated, Mr. Stoparic. Mr. Stoparic, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that is that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Jordash will now, as I understand for five minutes, continue his cross-examination. Has there been any discussions among the parties about the timing of today?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I understood Mr. Groome, he said he needs five minutes. I hope that nothing in my questions will increase that time so we are almost sure that we will be able to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber's questions, if any, will not take much time. So that's for your guidance. Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You told the Court a couple of days ago that you received a third salary directly from Boca; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you also said that this was paid -- this direct payment was also made to some other members of the Skorpions, not many of them; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And amongst the men who did, there were some who were related to them. Did the men who shot the unfortunate victims receive a similar personal payment from Medic? Were they amongst the number you were thinking about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How was it that you and -- well, let's stick with you. How was it that you were at the scene when the victims, the prisoners were delivered rather than being with the main a group of Skorpions at the front line or at the camp? Was there a reason for that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the front line together with another man, we went down to the base, and then we went to our communications centre to take over the recharged batteries for our communications equipment, and together with that, I also took a couple of bottles of fruit juice and some cigarettes and all I -- I was supposed to take all of those things to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I see. And the remainder, I think we dealt with this yesterday, but the remainder of the men including the perpetrators were there because they were -- would it be fair to describe them as more like personal aides to Medic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Aleksandar Vukovar was his official aide, he was responsible for the front line. But you are right, one could easily say about them that they were also some sort of aides.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Some of them even slept in Boca's -- where he was billeted, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they all slept in the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh. For any particular reason or just because they were on such friendly terms with Boca?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know their role was in the sense of being body guards, and if that indeed was the case, then it was only logical and normal for them to sleep close to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I just want to return very briefly, and I have only got a very few questions left, but to the issue that we left on yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we have on the e-court please, 1D1733.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you recall I put to you yesterday some testimony from the Belgrade court on the 12th of April, 2006, which suggested that at that point over four years ago you were of the mind that you had actually only seen the bus depart rather than it arrive and deliver the prisoners. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I probably answered somebody's questions over there. I can't tell you anything either approximately or exactly as to what I said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you want me to remind you or are you able to think about it now and give us your best evidence today? Could it be that you saw the bus departing rather than being there when it arrived or being there as it was parked?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not standing anywhere near the bus. The bus did not come to the cottages because there's no asphalt road there. I know the time when the bus appeared and when it left.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you a slightly different question then. Am I correct that you do not know who was on the bus other than, I think, approximately 15 prisoners? You didn't get a good sight of who was on the bus?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there were prisoners and some escorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, you believe that, but you didn't see it clearly, did you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance was 100 metres or perhaps a bit over, and that's the picture that I had before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I'm not criticizing you for that at all, but you don't know what happened to any of the people who were on the bus after it had departed leaving, the 15; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about 15. Why do you mention the number 15? I never mentioned it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, wasn't -- sorry, maybe that's my mistake. Isn't it the -- wasn't it the situation that there was 15 or so prisoners left, they were taken in a truck, and then six of them were taken out and executed. Is that not how it happened?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So it was just the six who were left by the bus; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because at that moment I did not count the men. I knew later there were six, but when they were first brought in, I didn't know. I didn't know whether there were six, seven, eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. But however many there were, they all were put into a truck and driven to their execution site; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were driven away by truck close to the place where they were killed. They had to walk for just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this event was a shock to you, it hadn't happened before amongst the Skorpions at Trnovo, had it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that was the first time ever that I learned about any such thing because even if I hadn't witness such events myself, I would have learned about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did the other Skorpions who were 2 to 5 kilometres away find out about this event, do you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, the same day. I would say even the same moment. The event had a domino effect, word-of-mouth messages spread very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And would you agree that there was general shock amongst the other Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it all depended on who heard the news. I don't know how to describe the prevalent feeling, whether it was shock or not. I can only say that I'm grateful to God to this very day that I was not the one who was ordered to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. And it never happened again, did it? This was a one-off event amongst the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately that is not the case. There was another event of that nature in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You mean the one in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just finally, I want to ask you about a comment or two in your 2005 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have P1703, please. And page 3 of the English and 3 of the B/C/S and also e-court, I think. Paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You can see there, just take your time to read it when the B/C/S comes, but of paragraph 9 says something a little odd maybe: "Boca then ordered the prisoners to be locked up." Could it -- have you orientated yourself with that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nine. I read 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, you can see that you put in your statement that Boca then ordered the prisoners to be locked up. Is that what happened in the first instance, Boca ordered the prisoners to be locked up?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the place used to be a garage as part of a weekend cottage and that's where they were temporarily placed and after that they were loaded on to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could it be that actually Boca ordered them to be locked up and then on the way to being locked up one of the perpetrators made the decision to kill them disobeying, in fact, Boca's order?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Finally, and I realise I've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, since we are at this page of 1703, the issue of the 15, whether that has never been said before, I just want to draw your attention to paragraph 12 of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. I will ask a couple of questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you see that in paragraph 12, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go to the next page of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Have a look at paragraph 12, and particularly --

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you see that? That's the 15. You see, that's another reason I ask you, Mr. Witness, whether in fact the decision was made by somebody who was in the truck as to who was going to be executed because, am I right, there was 15 people or thereabouts in the truck?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you that I didn't count them. I can't tell you whether there were six, seven, or eight, and here I can see that I used number 15. Believe me, as I sit here today I can't remember why, and there are only six men on the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I'm also -- because I'm not interfering, I left it to you how to divide your time, but the five minutes is --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I ask for two questions, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ask Mr. Bakrac, because it will be at the expense of his time, and therefore I leave it to you up to the moment where the Defence teams say, please Chamber divide the time for us, then we'll do that. But up to that moment, we leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, finally, you recall very clearly being employed by the Serbian MUP from August until December 1995; correct? I'm not disputing it.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I contest that. I did not work, I was a reservist. You used the word "work" which implies that I was active, but I wasn't, I was a reservist.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay, my fault. You were paid during that period, were you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. At the end of the last answer on line 17, the witness also mentioned a time-frame in answering Mr. Jordash's question. Unfortunately, I can't see that part of his answer in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see whether we can get it. You said, Mr. Stoparic: "You used the word 'work' which implies that I was active, but I wasn't, I was a reservist." And what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said at that time because Mr. Jordash did set a time-frame from the 11th of August up to -- I don't remember exactly when, but I confirm that that is the period in question. I agreed with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You were paid for that period; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were paid. I didn't know how often I was paid, and when the Prosecutor showed me the payroll, I realised that we were paid every fortnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you knew at that point very clearly you were being paid by the DB; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we were told we were reservists, I suppose that we were being paid by the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you made that supposition from August onwards, that you were being paid by the DB as a result of being a reservist?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jordash. Even if I said the MUP, I wouldn't be mistaken because it would still be the same ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, nothing further. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Let me just take the lectern from my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Bakrac is counsel for Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I didn't want to intervene into the transcript because I was about to start my cross-examination but let's deal with it now. When you were discussing pays on page 14 in answer to Mr. Jordash's question you said that as soon as you became a reserve member of a unit, and you mentioned which unit, and then you said which unit, and then you said that you supposed it was the DB that was paying you, so which unit was that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, let us go back a bit. Mr. Jordash has asked some of the questions that I meant to so I will start from 1992. From paragraph 58 of your statement, which is P1702.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we have that on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In paragraph 58 you say, and you testified about it yesterday, that you gathered a group of 200 volunteers and you decided that you would fight on the Brcko front; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there weren't 200 of them right away, but gradually we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But the rest is accurate, you decided that you would fight at the Brcko front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you fight at the Brcko front as part of that volunteer unit for the duration of 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how long we were there. I was coming and going. But I do believe that the period is entered into my military booklet. I don't know it by heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. We have it in evidence, we won't be wasting any more time. I'd like to hear from you whatever it is that you can remember. My next question, this volunteer group of yours which gradually grew to the number of 200, was it called the 7th Novi Sad Volunteer Company.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is how we called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Under whose command was this 7th Novi Sad Volunteer Unit in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paja Milinkovic was the brigade commander. I think it was the 2nd Posavina Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, let's look at two documents which might refresh your memory. Let's see if they have to do with you and your participation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 2D288.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know Colonel Borivoje Tesic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well the name sound familiar, Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were under the command of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have a look at this telegram. It reads -- so it's the Bratunac Brigade command sending it to the Drina Corps command on the 27th of November 1992. "I addressed you on several occasions for assistance in personnel from the perviously mentioned, 7th Novi Sad Volunteer Company, military post 7410/7 Brcko under the command of Lieutenant Goran Stoparic aka Sida. The company belongs to the Leva Supoderica Detachment whose command is under my command and in my area of responsibility with his personnel. I request that Lieutenant Sida, his personnel, and full equipment be transferred to my command post and placed under my command by Sunday at the latest. Unless the unit arrives, the Leva Supoderica Detachment will not be able to participate in the impending task." Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't mean that I was supposed to implement this order. May I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At some point, the Muslim forces under the command of Naser Oric broke through the lines in this area where Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic was present with the men from Vukovar who formerly belonged to this unit in 1991 as did I. So he learned that we were with the unit in Brcko, and he wrote to the command in Brcko with a request. However, I was never granted permission to leave an area which was equally complex as this one and I therefore never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But you do know of this corps by Borivoje Tesic for you to come from Brcko to their front line. You are aware of the fact that Leva Supoderica was under his command too. The only thing that you are telling us now is that you, in fact, did not go. So this request was not granted?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't down to me to decide about the request. It was up to the colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But for the remainder, the document is accurate, is it not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you said yesterday that the president of the municipality of Brcko offered citizenship of Republika Srpska to each and every men of your company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he brought along the appropriate forms where one needed to write one's particulars. It was a certified document and it was on that basis that we were entitled to be present in Republika Srpska rather than be a paramilitary group, and in this way we were immediately subordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska. And we received orders and participated in all the actions pursuant to their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you were subordinated to the Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a captain, a security officer that I took personally all these documents to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So it's late November, Lieutenant-Colonel Tesic is calling for you to come to the Drina Corps, but you remained in Brcko the whole of 1992, and will I be mistaken if I say 1993 as well?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, now that we are discussing Brcko, when you were testifying earlier on, you weren't sure if it was Pesa's unit or Zika Crnogorac's unit, you weren't sure if these were, in fact, two separate units or if one unit resulted from the other?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You also said that as for the unit of Zika Crnogorac you didn't know if it composed individuals from Serbia or locals from Bosnia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know them personally. There was just this one operation that lasted several hours. Pesa's unit I got to know better and they were all from Republika Srpska save from one individual who was from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me try and refresh your memory if I can. I can see in the transcript that there is a mention of General Tolimir, I didn't hear you say that at all. You said Pesa's unit and that all of his men were from Republika Srpska and one were from Croatia. Did you mention General Tolimir at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Now, it's corrected, Your Honour. That was my mistake. I apologise to the interpreters. Mr. Stoparic, can we look at 2D301 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please read this carefully. Tell us, since you were out in the field does this refresh your recollection in any way?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it not the case that a unit for special purposes of the MUP of Republika Srpska under the command of Zivojin Ivanovic, aka Zika Crnogorac, is being resubordinated to the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this refresh your memory? Was the unit of Zika Crnogorac known as the Special Purpose Unit of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew of them as specials or specialists of the MUP. It says here that it's the MUP of Republika Srpska, so there's no reason to doubt the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, and the document reflects something that you yourself can recall and that it has to do with Zika Crnogorac's unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they were specials of the MUP and perhaps some of them were from Serbia, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say MUP, you mean MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's perhaps the reason why I -- well, the reason why I don't feel the need to differentiate is the fact that at the time we were all living in one state.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's try and understand what you are saying. You don't feel the need to stress that it's the MUP of Republika Srpska because you felt that you were still living in one state, Yugoslavia, is that how I understood you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what, of course, is of interest, Mr. Bakrac, where the witness earlier said I've no reason to doubt that, whether apart from this document he has any knowledge which specifically addresses the matter on whether this unit was a MUP of Republika Srpska unit or a unit which was -- had to be related to the MUP of Serbia. That's the issue, isn't it? So let's ask the witness whether he has any specific knowledge on whether the unit belonged to the MUP of Serbia or to the MUP of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, I hope there's no need for me to repeat what His Honour has just said?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't even think about it. To be frank, I thought it was a unit belonging to the MUP of Serbia, and only now I see this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac. And do you have any reason which would support that belief? You said you believed it was the MUP of Serbia unit, is there any basis for that belief? Why did you believe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm almost certain that I wasn't the only one who held this view. Whenever serious individuals would arrive well-equipped and solemn-faced, we always thought that they were from Serbia, a state that was much better organised than was the case with Republika Srpska at the time. All the various events and ploys, et cetera, well that's the sort of thing that would cross one's mind and that was the case with me as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was therefore -- your belief was based on this impression, if I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I tender 2D301 into evidence, although it's in the bar table concerning Mr. Theunens and I think it was marked for identification. Well, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you have not addressed I think the previous document, 2D288, which is also among the remaining Theunens exhibits and has been provisionally assigned number D181 marked for identification. 2D301 is similarly now provisionally assigned number D187 marked for identification. Everything is now on the record, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, another question concerning Zika Ivanovic, Zika Crnogorac, if I'm right you said that he was in a sort of a conflict with local authorities. Is my understanding correct that this conflict was due to the fact that local authorities were responsible for some people leaving Brcko; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, something like that happened. I don't know the details but that was the general story which featured the name of Zika Crnogorac. What ultimately happened, somebody was driven out of Brcko. Somebody was expelled. I don't know who exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And Zika Crnogorac opposed this sort of contact, did he not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the particulars. I wasn't in any way involved in the conflict. We were simply told at the command that there was this problem there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't know on whose side Zika Crnogorac was. I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, did there come a time in spring 1993 that you fought on the side of the Croatian Defence Council against the Muslims in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not really proper to say that I was on their side. It would be properly said that I was acting in concerted action with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What does that mean in concerted action? Did you receive such an order from the Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Brcko for Teslic because that was the order I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can I stop you there. Who did you get the order from to go to Teslic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, who was the commander at the time. Perhaps Kutlasic or his deputy, I'm not sure. And I went to Teslic to the school there, which was also the base of the military police. That's where we spent the night and from there they drove us by vehicles along a minor road to a place called Zepca. In Teslic we were informed that we would act in concert with the Croatian Defence Council and that we should not display any hostilities towards them because we would be acting together, we would be working together. I spent about a month or less than a month there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who paid you while you were there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received my salaries at the Brcko barracks when I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce P1702. Paragraph 66. It's the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Paragraph 66 of your statement, Mr. Stoparic, there is a mismatch between that and what you said earlier today. It says here: "When I demobilised at Brcko sometime in the spring of 1993 ..." I don't know whether I understand the meaning of the word "demobilised" properly, that means that you left the army. And then you go on to say: "I took a few of the soldiers who shared similar beliefs as mine, and we went to Teslic to work with the HVO on a joint operation against the Muslims." You say here that you first demobilised and then that you took a few of the soldiers who shared your beliefs and that you did it of your own will and you joined the HVO.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not demobilised. I don't know, this is a bit confusing. After that I did demobilise. What beliefs are referred to herein. I have permuted something here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you shown this statement when you -- during your proofing session?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the Prosecutor did not show this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He didn't go through this statement?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did go through some statements, but I do not remember paragraph 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it possible that you only skimmed some of the paragraphs without ever trying to check or remember, you testifying here based on your prior statements, you provided some details arising from those. We see now that you have not studied your statements in detail.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I corrected what I thought I should correct, and this term "demobilised" should also be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be that I misspoke. I'm not perfect, am I?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. So what you are saying today, what you are testifying about today is the truth and what we see in paragraph 66 is not true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified in the Seselj case and I spoke about the same things and I testified in exactly the same way as today. There is a possibility that I made a mistake. I overlooked something or I forgotten things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Stoparic. Let's move on. You are here speaking about the spring of 1993. When we say spring 1993, can you tell us roughly which part of the spring of 1993 are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there was no snow there. I'm not sure about the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Stoparic. And as you testified today, a month after the operation in Teslic, you returned to Brcko and when were you demobilised?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, but the operation was not in Teslic but in Zepca.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, in Zepca. How much later after that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. The dates are my weak points.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And after Brcko where did you go, and we are still talking about the spring of 1993? Where did you go after Brcko?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. There were field missions where I spent only 15 days and returned. That's why it's very difficult for me to remember all the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Again as a member of the Posavina Brigade or the 7th Novi Sad Company?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 7th Novi Sad Company was disbanded, people scattered, there were no longer combat activities around the town of Brcko. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After Brcko you went back to Sid to your place of birth, right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there very often. I went for furloughs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did you join the Skorpion unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. As I sit here, I don't know. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was that in 1993, 1994? Maybe you can't remember the exact dates or perhaps even the exact month, but what year, what time of the year?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I am a bit confused now. What year? I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, you don't know you don't know. What can we do. Will you agree with me that -- and I believe you testified about that -- that the unit -- the Skorpion unit, it's organisation, it's relationship with other units, the issues of procurement, the issue of financing, knew about -- knew -- that Milan Milovanovic, Mrgud knew about all that better than you do.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. He should be the one to know absolutely everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, you also spoke about what you heard about the way the Skorpion unit was established. You spoke about that yesterday and the day before yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most difficult thing is to remember names. There was a meeting in Novi Sad and Zivko Sokolovacki and Milovanovic attending the meeting together with some other men. They decided to launch or relaunch the production of oil products and that a unit should be established to secure the fields. And that's how the unit was supposed to come into being.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from? Who did you hear about the unit, about the meeting, and about who attending the meeting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who the attendees were. I only remember Mr. Zivko Sokolovacki, I never saw the man. I also remember the name of Milan Milovanovic. I heard in the base when I joined the unit. The Skorpion unit already existed. I suppose that I asked somebody how the unit was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: A soldier?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An officer because I was never on sentry duty. I had other duties, other responsibilities. And the stories sounded plausible to me, sounded logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, you have just explained to us that Mrgud was the one who was best informed about the unit. You heard -- told us what you heard from others about the meeting. You had an opportunity to look at your statement and to make the necessary corrections in the statement, and you made a correction in paragraph 75 of the statement. First of all let me explain why I asked you when you joined the Skorpion unit. You said it was either in 1993 or 1994 but you are not sure; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot of things happened at the time so I really don't know and I didn't keep a diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In paragraph 75 you corrected something: "When I arrived there," and you say you are speaking about the Skorpion unit, "there were about 200 men in the Skorpions; 30 per cent were experienced, 30 per cent had no experience, and 30 per cent of the men came directly from the Red Berets trained in Kula and Tara, I'm referring to Frenki's Red Berets." And then you corrected something in that paragraph, and you said when you arrived there, there were 200 men in the Skorpions; 30 per cent were experienced, 30 per cent had no experience, and 30 per cent of the men had been trained in Frenki's camps for the Red Berets in Kula and Tara. Those men were not officially members of the Red Berets but they were trained in the Red Beret camps." Is that what you remembered a couple of days ago during your proofing session?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, 30 per cent of the men came from the Red Berets. And that's not correct. I was told that 30 per cent of the men had been trained, had completed training.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In Kula and Tara?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I can add to that that there was also Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: You corrected this on Monday, four days ago; right? And you are now claiming that 30 per cent of the Skorpions had arrived from Frenki's training centres for the Red Berets and you say that those centres were in Kula and Tara; do you adhere by that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not adhere by that. I said what I'd heard. I myself did not attend the trainings and then joined the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you be surprised, witness, if I told you that in 1993 and 1994 there was no training centre either in Kula or in Tara?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be surprised, no. But there must have been a training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So everything that you stated here is a matter of rumours or perhaps even the influence of the film that you watched before you provided a statement, and the film depicted a celebration in Kula which 1995 and 1996 became the base of the JSO. Can you we say that you were influenced by the film?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I watched the film a very long time ago and never again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But you did watch the film before you provided your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Belgrade. But I really don't know at what moment was that. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, sir, you heard rumours but you do not adhere by your statement because you don't know whether this is correct or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was told that 30 per cent of the men had been trained and the reference was made to Frenki and that nickname circulated around the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you were in front lines in Croatia or Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you also see Franko Simatovic also known as Frenki?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I saw him on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I know that you told us that you saw him on TV, but I'm asking you whether you ever saw him in person in Trnovo, in Croatia, in Bosnia, anywhere else in any other operation while you were a member of the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, there were rumours that the Red Berets were Frenki's Men; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were called Frenki's Men, not the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you saying that the Red Berets are one unit and Frenki's Men are a different unit; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Frenki's Men, that's how they were called. Sometimes the Red Berets, perhaps there are two units. I don't think that they are one in the same but I don't know. Very often a reference was made to Frenki's Men. That's what they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: However, based on that you concluded that that was the unit under Frenki's command. You don't have any information, any proof, any piece of evidence? You don't know any other fact that would point to that; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I first heard the nickname Frenki, I didn't know the name. I didn't know who was behind that nickname. It was only later that I learned that that was Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After you watched the movie; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, before that. The war was still going on. I don't know, maybe there was another Frenki just like there are several men known as Legija. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore you don't know when the nickname Frenki is mentioned, you don't know who is referred to by that nickname?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always thought that it was Mr. Simatovic, especially now that I know his family name. At first I thought that the reference was made to a very highly-positioned person in the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But when you heard Frenki's Men, how could you think that that was Mr. Simatovic if you say that you learned only later on that that was Mr. Simatovic when you saw him on TV?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said. I said that it was either him or somebody highly positioned in the state security, and it was later on that I related the nickname to the family name Simatovic when I heard it from other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say a highly positioned person in the state security, do you know as you sit today, what was Mr. Simatovic's position in the the state security from the very beginning until this very day or during the real relevant time, the time that we are talking about, do you know what his position was in the state security?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was an assistant to the chief. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Based on that, what do you base your answer on?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say. After a thousand television shows that spoke about all sorts of things, I believe that he was a high official, possibly a chief's assistant. A chief has many assistants, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, we have another five minutes before the break, let's look at something else. First of all, tell me while you were a Skorpion member, your commander was Slobodan Medic, also known as Boca; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, from the very beginning he was commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who Boca reported to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At times he would go to see generals of the VRS and to see the man Milan Milovanovic. He would also go to the government of that particular region, the SBWS, the head of government of some sort, and he would go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I apologise, when you say generals of the VRS, do you mean General Loncar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was the most recent general. He had predecessors. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know if Boca Medic reported to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who all the individuals were who he reported to. He would go to Sid every day. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is there anything like a fact, for instance, based on which you believe or think that Boca Medic reported to Franko Simatovic, Frenki?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he didn't report to him personally, but if it had to do with security issues, the reports may have reached that high up. I don't know. At any rate, I think they should have reached that far high because we are talking about armed men. If the reports didn't reach those quarters, at least they should have reached Milan Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, it is only an assumption of yours that unless it was those men from Sid, and Sid is close to the border with Croatia, at least Milovanovic would have received these reports and then if they went to the DB you wouldn't know who they eventually got to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I'm looking at the clock. We still have a minute left so I would move on. We have time enough for one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you reliably know which were the units that were on the DB payroll?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only legal official armed unit of the DB was the JSO as far as I know. For the rest, what you just said a moment ago would apply, that's to say that I don't have actual knowledge about them. What I can tell you that is absolutely true is the JSO -- I mean absolutely true, that's what I can tell with you absolute certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, one more question. It seems to me that you gave an example of a group of volunteers from Nis who wanted to join the Skorpions. You asked Medic about it and he explained it to you the following way: That he was told from the higher-ups that 60 per cent of the men should come from RS and RSK, and 40 per cent from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was roughly it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And he said that this had to be the case so that they could claim that those men from among them who were from Serbia were volunteers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But just confirm if this is right because I'm reading from a statement.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well that's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You are a native of Sid, are you not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you a volunteer in the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I joined upon an invitation from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So was it a misrepresentative fact that you were a volunteer from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, but the problem was that there were so many individuals coming from Serbia to the RSK; whereas, those from the RSK were dodging call-ups and fleeing to Serbia. In addition to that, Serbia was not at war. Well, I don't know, that's how he put it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that you, as a volunteer from Serbia, joined the Skorpions as did other individuals who were from Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. As for the ones from the the Krajina, they were in fact serving their military, compulsory military term whilst they were members of the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think I've overstepped my time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, Mr. Bakrac, and we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, let's continue. Before you joined the reservists, the JSO, in August of 1995, and while you were still in the Skorpions, did you have any joint actions that you undertook with the JSOs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When I say JSOs, I mean also the Red Berets and any joint actions with them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the time I was in the Skorpions, no, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that the Skorpions had some sort of uniform. Can you give us a description of were there two or three types of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And where did these uniforms come from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which factories they were delivered from.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me try and refresh your memory and then you'll tell me if it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D1731, 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it to appear on the screen, witness, is it true that on the 7th of July, 2005, you spoke with the investigating judge of the Special Council for War Crimes Stuparic here in The Hague concerning the crimes committed by Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was an investigating judge, I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have 0466-8362. That's the ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this, Mr. Stoparic, let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can counsel please refer to e-court page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it's page 7 in B/C/S. I can't find the page number in English. Yeah, the page in B/C/S is the accurate one. I think it's page 8 in English. It's the page before in English, so page 7 in English as well. I suppose that's why my assistant didn't write it down. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the investigating judge asked you about where the supplies of uniform had arrived and your answer is: "I know about a transfer of uniforms brought by a trader from Sid. He was of course paid for his work. He would frequently be buying them for the Skorpions, and this was Slobodan Medic's private connection and personal acquaintance with the man. In this way both of them were able to earn money." Then he went on to ask you about the caps that you had, et cetera. So does this refresh your memory? Is what I read out correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The man mentioned here, well, it was actually his company. I even remember it's name. I can give it to you, if you want. Almost always he would be the one providing all the foodstuffs that we needed, everything went through him. I also remember him bringing uniforms on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So all of it was a private arrangement by Boca Medic who earned a hefty sum through this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I even know that after the Erdut agreement, the men sued him for a commercial transaction for which he had not been paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you go to a battle-field in Bosnia as a member of the Skorpions, and if so, where and for how long?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went to the Bihac front line to the Cazina -- Cazinska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's take the Bihac front line first. Do you recall when you went there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who ordered you to go to the Bihac front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I sit here, no. I was given the order by Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who ordered Medic to go to the Bihac front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it was the command. I can't remember. I don't know who issued the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say the command, who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Republika Srpska Krajina. I think that the villages around Bihac also belonged to a Krajina, but not this one, but the other one on the other side, and I think that both Krajinas were actually one whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say the command of Republika Srpska Krajina, you mean its military command?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't tell you. I think they, the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How long did you spend at the Bihac front line with the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What does that mean, not much? How long?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one normally went on field missions for a month and I think that this was under a month, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know at all if Mr. Frenki Simatovic had any role to play or anything to do with the action in Bihac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was around Bihac, not in Bihac proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, around Bihac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there were any special units of the MUP or the Red Berets there. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When I asked you a moment ago you said that you had never taken part in any action with the JSOs or the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's true. Taking part is one thing. We could have a large area. For instance, I was in Kosovo but I didn't participate in an action with the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But even now you don't know at all if the Red Berets had a part to play in the Bihac front line or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's been a long time and I can't tell you one way or another. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, did you see Franko Simatovic in that front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said earlier on that I had not seen Mr. Frenki Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the other operation in Bosnia which was the one in Velika Kladusa. Who ordered you to go to Velika Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we were told that the action in Velika Kladusa was a result of an initiative from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us be precise here. The only thing you remember is being told that this was an initiative from Belgrade, but you don't know who it originated from, do you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I don't know. I can't give you a name. From Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us who told you that the initiative came from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, the reconnaissance the platoon were lined up, and Medic would always talk to us more than the other ones in the two companies because we would always go out into the field; whereas, the other companies would alternate. And he said that there would be other units over there participating as well as units from the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Republika Srpska, and we the Skorpions. We were also told that most of the other special units would be involved as well. I don't recall exactly, but I think it was the 5th Corps which attacked the army of Fikret Abdic and that it even captured some of the territories there. And we were supposed to rectify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you were asked who told you that the initiative came from Belgrade? You started your answer by: "We, the reconnaissance platoon were lined up, and Medic would always talk to us more than the others." Do I understand this that Medic told you that it was a Belgrade initiative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, for not rounding off my thought. Well, of course, yes, Medic was the one. Medic told us so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, unless you would have on your mind to ask all the questions the witness already answered, I would have stopped him after the first or the second line. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, how long did you stay in Velika Kladusa on the front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long. We were all poisoned. We contracted diptheria, dysentery or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did somebody come to bring you back to Djeletovci?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have been Mrgud. We were waiting for a day or two suffering until the men from another unit came and filled our places.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While you were there for a month or so, did you see Franko Simatovic? Did you know anything about his role in the Velika Kladusa Operation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see Mr. Simatovic. And if you would allow me to drop some names, some more prominent names, I saw Ulemek. He came to the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say Ulemek, you mean Legija?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say Ulemek, you are talking about the year 1994, do you know which unit did Ulemek belong in 1994, and again I'm talking about Legija?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know much about his history. Actually, I do, because it's public knowledge at the moment. I know that he was a member of Arkan's Tigers and that he was also a member of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So first he was a member of Arkan's Tigers and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters asked the witness to repeat what he said. You started by saying: "I know that he was a member of Arkan's Tigers and that he was also a member of --" And then could you repeat what you then said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I know that he was a member of Arkan's Tigers, as well as JSOs after that. He was even their commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that Ulemek, Legija, was transferred to the JSO after 1995?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for a fact when that happened, in what year. I'm not entirely sure about that. However, I know that during his first Balkan adventure, he was a member of Arkan's Tigers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you said that while you were in Velika Kladusa participating in that operation until you all got ill you saw only Legija of all the prominent figures. Do you know who was in command of Skorpions during that operation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. My commander was Medic and I don't know who his superior was. I know that Radojica Bozovic was mentioned but I didn't see him. I think he was supposed to be there as well. He may have been his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you heard stories, you heard that he was supposed to be there but you don't know whether he was Medic's commander or not. You only heard that a certain person, Radojica Bozovic was there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, maybe Legija was in a higher position than Medic. Maybe he was a higher ranking officer. There was also the command of Abdic's army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of General Mile Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you be surprised if I told you that General Mile Novakovic was the Pauk commander and that the Chief of Staff was Cedo Bulat?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Cedo Bulat, but I know that Mile Novakovic was the commander of Pauk and he was supposed to be replaced by Manojlo Manojlovic perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And your unit as well as all the other units were all subordinated to Mile Novakovic, right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if Mr. Mile Novakovic who was a general and he was a commander, I suppose that all units were subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stoparic. So those were the two operations in Bosnia. And now I would like to draw your attention to the operation around Sarajevo, rather around Trnovo. Kindly tell us about that operation. Who was it who issued an order for you to march towards Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Manojlovic brought Loncar's order to the office at one point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, when you say Manojlovic, which Manojlovic do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srdjan Manojlovic. He was an assistant commander. He was an active officer in the former JNA, or perhaps a non-commissioned officer. I'm not sure. In any case, he had graduated from a military school and after that he joined the Skorpions and he worked in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say deputy commander, you mean the Skorpion commander Boca Medic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And when you say that he brought an order from Loncar, you mean General Loncar who at the time was a general in the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure whether his headquarters was Beli Manastir or in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Stoparic, when you arrived in the Trnovo theatre of war, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again a month. I don't know exactly to be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, which units did you personally see, did you personally encounter in that theatre of war besides the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the Trnovo theatre of war, I'm going to tell you what I saw when I was on the separation line, or rather on the front line. On my right there was a unit from a town in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'll try and jog your memory. Was that unit from the Zvornik Brigade or the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either or, one of the two I believe so, yes. And that was on my right-hand side. I don't remember who was on my left flank. I remember those men whom I called the CSB Doboj unit. There were also some other specials, when I say "specials" I mean people in NATO uniforms, but I didn't see them on the front line actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's summarise. You saw two units on the front line, one of them was either from the Zvornik or the Bratunac Brigade and you also saw the CSB Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were specials from Doboj whose commander was a man referred to everybody by the name of Zenga.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And that was a unit from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For the Trial Chamber and for the benefit of everybody else we have to clarify, the Zvornik or the Bratunac Brigade were also units from Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a few of their members and, yes, they are from Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you also said that you had seen a few special, where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was passing through Trnovo I saw jeeps, jeep vehicles. And on one occasion I was on foot escorting the commander and we were walking to a hotel on Mount Jahorina. Actually, we were walking along is a ski slope. I saw cable cars and there I saw a large group of specials and Medic went there to a meeting, to attend a meeting there, and I heard that Mr. Simatovic was also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who told you that? Who told you that Mr. Simatovic was there at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Medic and his other escorts. Although we were not allowed to go there, only Medic went up there to that hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did Medic tell you personally that he had seen Franko Simatovic there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the same road back and he went back by jeep. Somebody must have brought it to him, and he never told me that he had met with Simatovic. He mentioned somebody by the name of Kobac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, he didn't tell you that he was supposed to meet Mr. Franko Simatovic? I'll ask you again, did you personally see Franko Simatovic in Trnovo in the Sarajevo front line during the month that you were there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Mr. Simatovic was in that hotel at the time, I was there only once, and after that I was on the front line all the time and I didn't see him, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Since you say that Boca Medic didn't tell you that he was supposed to meet Simatovic, how do you -- just bear with me for a moment, please. Who did you hear it from about Franko Simatovic being on Mount Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I try to explain, maybe I didn't put my words properly. When we were walking up that ski path Boca told us, I'm off to a meeting, Frenki is there. Whether he ever met Frenki or not he didn't tell me because I didn't see him on that day, and that same evening or perhaps the following morning, I was sent to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And that's the only piece of information that you had about the presence of Franko Simatovic, Frenki, on Mount Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's not. There were other men, Zenga's men who also told us that that guy Frenki was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where did they tell you that? Who told you that? Which of the Zenga's men?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can describe a situation. I can give you anecdotal evidence which may not be that anecdotal for ordinary people. We went on a mission to scour the forest ground and we didn't know that Zenga unit was ahead of us and they managed to destroy a bunker. There were a few BiH Army soldiers in that bunker and they killed them in combat. Five or six minutes later, we arrived on the spot. We had heard shooting and then we arrived at the bunker. Our entire reconnaissance platoon was there and Medic was with us. And why I remember all of that, I remember it because one of the soldiers cut off the head from the dead body and put it in his rucksack, and then he told one of my soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, unless you wanted to say that he then told one of your soldiers that he had seen Frenki, the question simply was: Which of Zenga's men told you that Frenki was there? Could you identify him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The guy who had cut the head off told us that he was going to throw that head on to Frenki's desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say the person who told you was someone who you saw when a bunker was taken and where this person said that he would put the cut off head of a killed person on Frenki's desk, that's the answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the next question is why would you think Frenki's desk would indicate that Frenki was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not what I think. I'm just telling you what he said. He said that the head that he had in his rucksack, that he would throw it on to Frenki's desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that doesn't say anything about whether Frenki was present there or whether he would put it on Frenki's desk in Belgrade or in wherever. He didn't say that Frenki's desk at that time was on Mount Jahorina, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm simply telling you when, at what moment and under what circumstances I heard a reference to that nickname Frenki. And I thought that he was somewhere around in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's clearly distinguish between the presence of Frenki and a reference to Frenki by his nickname. I do understand that, I take it then from what you earlier told us, that you believed that Frenki was around because that was what Medic had told you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, could you please tell me first of all do you know whether that person did indeed take that head and throw it on to Frenki's desk?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps he did, perhaps he did not. I don't know. Maybe he was just a madman. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell me approximately the time when he told you in relation to that event involving those persons when you arrived, can you remember the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that. Before that event, a day or two after we arrived in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Stoparic, I'm going to ask you again, in Trnovo and Mount Jahorina for the month that you were there, you personally did not see Mr. Simatovic even for a brief moment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I repeated it already a hundred times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce P1702, paragraph 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I'm going to start reading very slowly while the document is being brought up. While waiting for paragraph 100 to be displayed, you say: "When the Skorpions went to Sarajevo, we were located at Trnovo, a small village under Treskavica mountain near Sarajevo. The joint MUP/DB command run by Frenki was at the Jahorina hotel on Jahorina mountain. I would come with Boca there and I see Rajo Bozovic, Frenki, in passing, Rambo, some of Arkan's Men whom I knew, and others. I did not see Legija there." So what's correct? Is it true that you saw Frenki as you stated in your statement, or what you have just told us for an umpteenth time that you didn't see Frenki?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see Frenki.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, this however raises the issue where you so specifically stated that you saw Rajo Bozovic, Frenki, in passing, Rambo, and you mentioned some of Arkan's guys. And then you said I did not see Legija there. Why did you so positively state at the time, not only by saying who you saw but also who you did not see there, that you had seen Frenki?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I say that I didn't see Legija there it means that somebody asked me if I had seen Legija. As for Frenki, I'm 100 per cent sure I didn't see him. I saw some of the Arkan's Men --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you here. I'm not asking you what you just said, but why at the time you said not only that you did see Frenki but also how you saw him, that is in passing, which now apparently is not accurate, and you did not correct it when you reviewed your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I must have overlooked it. Maybe that's an error on my part, but it wasn't deliberate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, is the name of Vaso Mijovic familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is familiar. I think that the man was there as well, though I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me, since you said that you remembered that there was the Zvornik or the Bratunac Brigade, if I suggested that Vaso Mijovic was perhaps within the perimeter of the Zvornik or Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name sounds familiar. I think he was there but I can't precisely tell you which unit and brigade he belonged to, where he served. The name is familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
