utterances.text: Did Vaso Mijovic act as commander to you, the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, frankly, even if I had met him, I would not have known that it was him. I don't know, maybe he did. Do you mean to say that he was superior to Boca Medic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know anything about it at all? If you don't, tell us you don't.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if he was the man, but most definitely Medic was not at the top. He was not the top superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that General Milosevic of the Army of Republika Srpska was in command of these operations at Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I heard his name but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which allows me for perhaps the time for another question. You earlier told us that you did not know whether this person who said who I would throw a head on Frenki's desk whether he did so or not. However, in your statement, and I read it to you: "One of the guys in that unit through a head of a dead Muslim soldier on Frenki's table at his Jahorina headquarters." So you do not only state that he did but you even indicate at what he location this was done. Could you explain to us why with this detail you told at the time that this person did throw it on Frenki's table, and whereas you now say: "I don't know, perhaps he did, perhaps he did not, I don't know. Maybe he was just a madman, I don't know." What is the basis for what you stated as to this head of the Muslim being thrown on Frenki's table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly gave the statement several years back and perhaps I had a better memory, but you've reminded me now that in fact it was said that the man did as much, did as he promised, that he threw that severed head on the desk in the command office of -- at Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And who told you that, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. When he said that he would be doing that for the first time, it was in the presence of everyone. And then probably somebody must have subsequently told us that he in fact did as promised. I can't tell you that I saw him throw it on the desk, but I did see the head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this was told to you when you were still in Trnovo or in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the feedback you received did not come from the man who promised that he would do such a thing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And in answer to my explicit question, you explicitly said that he promised that he would do so, but now that this statement was read back to you, you remember that you heard the feedback?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he didn't only tell this to me. There were 40 other people present.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, can you give us a name or two of those who were present during that event, and if you want us to, we can go into private session?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all of the scouts were presents as well as Medic in the company of five or six of his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, let me stop you there. The clock is ticking and we don't have much time. Can you give me names of the Skorpion members who were with you and who heard this and who are still alive today?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of the Skorpions called Darko Miljkovic was the one who opened up the rucksack. Medic saw it. I did. Milovan Stojic did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who heard the individual say that he would throw the item on to Frenki's desk? I'm not asking you about who saw it but who heard it? Did all of them hear it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of the ones I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And did they all hear the feedback about him having done as much?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if all of them heard the information, but we were altogether while discussing it and we were discussing it ironically.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say ironically, you meant that in fact you were making fun of it; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, do you know an individual by the nickname of Cena, the name being Goran Sehovac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the family same Sehovac and I know, and I saw several individuals bearing that surname. As for Cena, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You don't know Goran Sehovac, commander of the special unit of the MUP from Sarajevo? You don't know him from the Trnovo front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that there is typing noise to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before you left Trnovo and Jahorina, do you know --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: -- from the Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branislav.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you recall a celebration at Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the interpreters did not catch the name. When you asked: "Before you left Trnovo and Jahorina, do you know --" And what name did you then mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I mentioned a name. I asked about a celebration. If Mr. Stoparic remembered before leaving Trnovo and the Sarajevo front line, if there was a celebration of some sorts organised at Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Mr. Bakrac, the answer of the witness was Branislav, so I don't know think that that was an answer to before you left Trnovo and Jahorina was there a celebration. His answer was Branislav, so I don't know what you asked him, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was an interpretation error. I didn't hear him say Branislav, he said "proslava," meaning celebration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then this may resolve the matter. So you asked about a celebration before the witness left Trnovo and Jahorina. Then still from the Sarajevo area, is that before he left from the Sarajevo area, to have to understand it that way, and not as a person being from that area. I think I understood it. Did you attend a celebration, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember attending a celebration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And did you hear of one before you left Trnovo and the Sarajevo front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever say that after the fall of Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde, did you ever hear of a celebration taking place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after the fall of Srebrenica, Gorazde, and Zepa, everybody was celebrating in the military sense, that's to say a military victory was being celebrated. Nobody was thinking about Srebrenica with a different connotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So in other words, there wasn't a celebration in a specific place, rather there was general merriment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if there was a celebration party somewhere, then it must have been attended by Medic. I celebrated it with my fellow soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did Medic tell you of a celebration that he was going to attend at hotel Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you review your statement four days ago or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, paragraph 104 you say: "News arrived about the fall of the enclaves of Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde, and then Boca told us that the main purpose of the operation was for troops to move in, and there was a celebration where there was Frenki, Bozovic, and Zenga. I was not there, I was holding our lines against a Muslim counter-attack." So can you remember, was there a celebration or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that the action's purpose was to draw forces away from those places, well, that's what the commander told me. As for the celebration, the commander did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bakrac, already a page earlier, you could have just asked the witness what apparently you want to know. In paragraph 104 you state that there was a celebration at the Jahorina hotel and that Frenki and Bozovic and Zenga were present. Now, what's the basis of your knowledge where you now apparently do not have any recollection to any celebration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I can't memorise such voluminous material in one day. I have this block. I have this mental block and I'm not Nikola Tesla, you know. I'm just an average person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you don't have to memorise anything. What I'm asking you is you stated that there was a celebration and that Frenki was present. Today you say you have no recollection of that. Now, is it that you know there was no celebration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In answer to the counsel's question, I said that I didn't remember and I find it difficult to remember, that's it. I know that there was general celebration of the victory over the enclaves, but simply I don't know what to tell you. I simply didn't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you don't remember a celebration. Is it your recollection or do you not have any recollection as to the presence of Frenki at such a celebration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that this was read out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, if it refreshes your recollection of what you said, fine, but if you don't remember even -- I mean, I do not invite you to remember things that you really do not remember. If you say this refreshes my recollection and I now do remember, fine. But if you say I really don't remember even while reading this, well, I understand what I may have said at the time but I still do not remember, please tell us. I am not inviting you to remember anything just because you think we might like you to confirm what is in your statement. Do you have any recollection either after your memory was refreshed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to stick to the answer that I gave to the lawyer. I remember that I celebrated together with my soldiers and as for the other details, I really can't remember them as I sit here today. If I said something like that seven or eight years ago, maybe my memory was better at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you gave that statement, did at any moment did you intentionally not tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's nothing for me to intentionally not say. I can say something that perhaps is not true, but I believe it is true and the entire string of events and the entire picture may prove me wrong but that was my perception of the things at the time. I don't know if you appreciate what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, when you returned from the Trnovo front line, you went to Sid, right, and if I understood you properly a member of the state security from Sid recommended you for training at the Tara camp belonging to the JSO; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that member gave me the telephone number and told me if you want to go there, go to Jahorina hotel, ask them to give you a telephone, ring, somebody will come and fetch you there, and they'll take you there. And that's how things transpired.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So who did you call, Jahorina hotel at Tara?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I apologise, Omorika hotel, I was at Omorika hotel and from there, from the front desk I called that number, and then a vehicle came, a Lada Niva came and a policeman in it, and they took me to Tara hotel, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And did you perceive that as a police training facility?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the person working at the front desk of the hotel was a policeman. There were very few of us there. I was there for a one day or two before another group joined us and then a person came in civilian clothes and a leather jacket and called my name. Before that I handed over all of my documents and then he told me this, I can see that you -- I don't know how to explain that. I see that you are idol. While you are waiting for the group to arrive, I can see that you are a lieutenant, why don't you go to the field and exercise, or rather, train others? And that's what happened, for two days I was in charge of the physical training and then a middle-aged man came and he replaced me. There were quite a few different men who didn't have a clue. They only knew how to put a bullet in a rifle. They didn't know about the communications means or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What was the name of that person who trained you and for how long did he train you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, we were waiting for a certain number of people to gather and as for the name of that person, I only know that he was a local. He resided not far from there. He was raised on a little town not far from there. That's what I remember. He wore a uniform. He was a professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What kind of a uniform, a regular police blue uniform?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, a NATO uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How long were you there in training?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long. I don't remember, maybe a week, not longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you don't remember the name of the person who trained you for a week?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember. Actually, I don't think I ever knew his family name, but he did introduce himself by -- himself by his first name. I only remember that he lived in a little town not far from the hotel but I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Franko Simatovic while you were at that training centre at Tara, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, when you left the Skorpions, that's something I skipped, and I want to follow the proper chronology. On the 11th of August you joined the JSO in the way that you've just described. What did you do with the weapons that you had been provided with from the Skorpion unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Skorpion unit, I handed the weapon over. I gave it back to the Skorpion base.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The Skorpion base in Djeletovci; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that everything was loaded on to trucks and driven to the Sid barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say the Sid barrack, you mean the military barracks, the barracks belonging to the army; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time the military had already been established, the border was there, and the barracks as well. And that was on the road between Sid and Tovarnik. And all the lorries carrying the Skorpion equipment went there and were offloaded there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the 11th of August, as you say, and we'll go back to the certificate confirming that, when you joined the JSO, did you sign a contract with anybody in confirmation that you were joining JSO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but that man, the instructor promised to those of us who were good that they would have an opportunity to sign, to be properly activated, but that was to happen after our first field mission but that never materialised. Nobody signed any contracts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That means that you did not sign any contracts despite the promise that had been made to you that contracts would be signed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, a lot of us asked whether that would happen because according to my military logic, the -- that would have been the top of my career. If I were to become a member of such a unit, I would have quite a huge professional satisfaction because there was a lot to be learned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. I was just interested in this. You were told that you had signed contracts but no contracts were signed. It was just a promise?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that man told us that those who were good first for a period of half a year, then two or three years, I can't remember exactly for how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, let's look at another paragraph in the statement and then we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1702 again. I believe that it is still on the screen although I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I'm looking at the clock. We are about at the time that we have a break. Could I inquire as to how much time you would need after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, 30 to 40 minutes tops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore if do you it in 30 minutes, then there would be sufficient time for Mr. Groome to ask further questions and for the Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Estimate about eight minutes at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Eight minutes at this stage. We have 75 minutes after the break. Mr. Jordash as matters stand now, do you think that you would have -- of course, you do not know what questions will be raised by Mr. Groome, but let's see that you finish in 35 minutes after the break, Mr. Bakrac, yes, that would be good, and I also advise you to stop the witness if he is giving you a lot of answers on questions you never asked him because that takes a lot of time and you can stop him and take him back to the question which --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hesitate when it comes to doing that because sometimes you reprimanded me for not allowing the witness to finish his answer so now I'm cautious and hesitant, but in any case I'll try and see what I can do about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's good to be cautious and sometimes to be hesitant. At the same time, it takes a lot of time to listen to answers on matters that you have asked no questions about. We'll have a break and we'll resume at a quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, until 25 minutes past. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could the Court please produce paragraph 109.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for paragraph 109 to appear on the screen, witness, we mentioned contracts, I'm going to start reading the paragraph which is quite long. You say: "After I left the Skorpions, I was in Sid." You spoke to an inspector, you spoke about Tara Mountain and where you went, and then you say as follows: "We became members of the JSO. When my name was called out, it appeared that they knew about my past in the DB's Skorpion unit. They knew my rank and had probably done a background check. I signed a six-month contract, and then after a few months I signed a three-year contract with the Red Berets/JSO. In the contract the unit was called a JSO, the special operations unit of the Serbian DB. And the contract bore the insignia of the 4 Ss with a sword and a wolf. It also featured the stamp of the JSO." You had an opportunity to review this statement four days ago, which is correct, did you sign the contract or did you not? In this statement you even describe the contract.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I corrected this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where did you correct this? We have not been notified about any corrections to this effect?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I corrected this with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did you correct this with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, two or three days ago, I would say. Three days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe he is referring to P1704, the second page where it says paragraph 109. Those are the corrections he made to this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could P1704 be displayed on the screen. We would like to see the correction. I may be mistaken, but the way I read this, I don't see this as a correction. Can the second page be displayed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, the second page of P1704, for me it's a one-page document, and it's the famous document referring to the 11th of June this one page, that's P1704.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My record is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please let me check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is on the screen now, Your Honour, is what I have as P1704, it's the corrections to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I may have made a mistake in getting it. Yes, I made a mistake, I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm looking at the document again, I've seen it before, but I don't see this as a correction or as a claim that he didn't sign anything. Let's clarify with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It says here: "Everybody who successfully underwent the training had an opportunity to sign a six-month contract. If they had been good in training after the sixth month, they would be offered a three-year contract with the Serbian MUP." Mr. Stoparic, how come that in 2003 you described the contract that you allegedly signed with the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person, and I repeated that in my statement, that person told us that we would have an opportunity to sign a six-month contract and then a longer term contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, I'm pressed for time, in your statement of 2003 you said that you did sign the contract and you even described the contract, and you say the contract featured 4 Ss, a sign with a sword and a wolf, as well as a JSO stamp. Why did you say that in 2003? Why did you describe the contract that you allegedly signed with the JSO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not sign a contract. That's why I corrected my statement, and here I describe a contract that I saw somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where did you see the contract?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody had it at Tara. I believe that that man showed the contract to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, in 2003 you didn't remember that, and now in 2010 you remember that you actually did not sign the contract but that that person at the Tara camp actually showed you what the contract looked like, is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Court please produce P1708.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, and while we are waiting for the document to be displayed, let me tell you that this is a certificate which says that between the 11th of August to 22nd December 1995, you were engaged by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia and that you performed certain tasks and duties. I have a couple of questions with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could Mr. Stoparic have the benefit of having a closer look at the stamp. At the signature. Could that be blown up for Mr. Stoparic's benefit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, first of all tell me, do you know who Stojan Petrovic is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you got this certificate?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the name of the place is either Pajdos or Pajzos near Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did you receive this certificate?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that I received it on the 22nd of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We will display the top of the page in a minute. Look at the stamp, does it say "special purpose unit" rather than "special operations unit"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very illegible. Actually, just the word "unit" is legible and "purpose" is legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that you were a member of the JSO, and here we see that a person called Stojan Petrovic signed the certificate testifying that you were a member of the special purpose unit. How can you account for that difference?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I never paid any attention to that. I'm looking at this stamp for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would it be of any assistance if I told you that the special purpose unit was under the public security centre?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, can we scroll up to the top of the page for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It seems, Mr. Stoparic, that you received this certificate on the 12th of December and not on the 22nd of December. You had just told us that you received it on the 22nd of December?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a categorical statement. I just read up to 22nd and I believed fully that that was the day when the certificate was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And how do you account for the fact that it was issued earlier than the 22nd. How did they know that you would stay with the unit until the 22nd of December if it was only the 12th of December?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state with full responsibility as soon as I received this certificate, when I had already handed back my weapons, my uniform, everything, and at that same moment I got on a bus and went to Sid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excellent. Thank you, Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up 2D152, please. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask one question first. Looking at this stamp there are few letters which are clearly decipherable. Is there, and I take it if you would look at the original, and if you would be someone who would be a native speaking -- a native B/C/S speaking person, then I consider it likely that finally one could agree on the text on it, but I would like to know whether there's any dispute about what the stamp reads. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the official translation of this document, the person has put -- the native speaker has put a question mark, which usually indicates their uncertainty about the legibility of it, so I wouldn't be able to agree given that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, and therefore I asked. Apparently the person who translated it was hesitant to -- but therefore, of course, what you would do then is perhaps not ask someone who translates primarily but who would look closer to the stamp to see whether the text can be deciphered. I mean, there are relatively simple methods for doing that. Often I would just wonder whether there's any disagreement -- I beg your pardon, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting you, Your Honour, but perhaps the witness may be of assistance. It is his certificate. He can read the original and maybe he can make out what the stamp says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not mind if we ask the witness, but to say how the witness interprets it would be decisive for me would be too far a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Court wishes, I could ask the Netherlands forensic institute to examine the original. They may have special equipment that would allow them to enhance the visibility of the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If ordinary means would not finally resolve the matter then one could consider that. I'm not immediately thinking about experts, but I would first of all start with a common-sense approach, that is to perhaps use a different light which very often gives already a clue to where ink is found and not without even hiring an expert on it. So to see whether you would agree on that, whereas at least the interpreter found it clear enough to give it at least a try or to -- that's at least what I understand it to be, that the interpreter considered it most likely this text which is more than illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the other thing that maybe Mr. Bakrac and myself could work on over the break is to identify other documents that have both examples of special operations unit, special purpose unit, and to see whether the font is the same or to see whether that sheds light on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For example, that's exactly the kind of common-sense approach I would start with before hiring experts. Then the original, you'll carefully keep it, Mr. Groome, for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's in the safe, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I agree with my learned friend Mr. Groome, but I then suggest that this document be marked for identification. Since the stamp is in dispute, I think it would be reasonable to keep it as an MFI at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's the status it has and I -- isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think I would disagree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll check. If it is MFI'd until now, then no one has applied for changing the status. If it's not being MFI'd, then we might reconsider whether, but I have to check that. I can easily do that, one second. Yes, it is MFI'd, as I thought. It keeps that status for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we now call up Exhibit 2D152.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, look at this ID and tell me if it's the sort of ID you received when you were a member of the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it opened in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, in addition to that, can you tell me this, I'm putting it to you that this is a dark blue booklet. Was this the sort you had in the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't look that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My second question this: When you said that a DB official from Sid showed you his ID for a brief moment, is this what this DB official's booklet looked like?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it did have a large coat of arms, it did say official identity card, so yes, that could be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did it stay state security?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have it in my hands. The man showed it to me, introduced himself, and said sit down. But it did have the state coat of arms, it did read official ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But do you recall if it said state security at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the man was most certainly from state security. I didn't have any doubts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Don't think about that. I'm asking you if the ID said state security?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. If you don't, that's how it is. Mr. Stoparic, as a member of the Skorpions, you were also deployed at Kosovo in Podujevo were you not in 1999?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just Podujevo, but, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did Milan Milanovic, aka Mrgud, accompany you to Prolom Banja on your way to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did Milan Milanovic Mrgud find accommodation for you at a hotel in Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I put it to you that Milan Milanovic, aka Mrgud, accompanied you from Belgrade from Makis stadium and that he did not go on from there, did not accompany the Skorpions from that point onwards, what would your answer be?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say anything. I am convinced that he did accompany us from that point on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Stoparic, you gave two more statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we call up Exhibit 1D1720. Can we look at paragraphs 105 through 108, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you said earlier on in reference to some discrepancy that you were not Nikola Tesla, you are just an average man with no sophisticated knowledge, that you wanted to summarise things. Now, what I'm going to do is I am going to read what you say from paragraphs 105 to 108. You say as follows: "I will briefly explain the reasons which made me take this insane step. At the time there was unprecedented propaganda in our media about a resurgent Ustasha ideology in Croatia. We were told that the lives and personal properties of the Serbs in Croatia were threatened, that one-third of the Serbs would be killed, one-third expelled, and one-third converted to Catholicism. Of course, at the time I was very young and I did not try to think about it but rather just believed what I was told. "The politicians managed in a very perfidious way to awaken chauvinism and to convince us of the necessity to have all Serbs living in one state. They managed to make us see the desire of some FRY republics to become independent and exist outside Yugoslavia as an anti-Serbian act and a possible genocide against the Serbs. In their public appearances, they reminded us of Second World War events, for instance, Jasenovac and other execution sites of the Serbs. At that time, Slobodan Milosevic took the initiative. Later, Vojislav Seselj's era came, even Vuk Draskovic's, not to mention the others. Personally, I either did not want to or I did not have enough intelligence to keep away from the horrible events that were to unfold. I'm a perfectly average man with secondary school education; hence, I cannot reproach myself that much, even now, for becoming part of Slobodan Milosevic's monstrous global plan." Mr. Stoparic, what I just read out, are these your own words?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote it myself. The Prosecutor should have a manuscript with my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You gave this to the Prosecutor in writing before you actually had the interview, did you not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sat down at a desk one night and wrote it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does the Prosecutor have this? You handed it over to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not to this Prosecutor sitting here. To someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. So, witness, you prepared this ahead of your interview with the Prosecutors and brought it along?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain it this way: After what do you call it, a briefing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, Mr. Bakrac is going to ask you a question and then would you please answer the question. Otherwise the same happens as we experienced before. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, before you signed this statement, before it was made did you bring this section as an notation that you wrote beforehand?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was that evening before my meeting with the investigator that I wrote it and then brought it along the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This handwritten note was not disclosed to us. I suppose Mr. Groome doesn't have it or he would have disclosed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D1724.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the statement we were looking at just now was given between February 2004 and November 2005, and now I'll be showing you a statement which was given in 2006 on the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th of August in The Hague. There is no need for me to read from paragraphs 4 through 7. Mr. Stoparic, have a look. We can all have a look. So paragraphs 4, 5, 6 are identical to the other ones. So did you produce that piece of paper again in 2006 or was it investigators copying what you said in your earlier statement, or did you simply dictate it from memory to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell them this from memory. It was just something I wrote one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So did you write it again a year later? How is it possible for these same words to find their way into a statement you gave a year later?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't rewrite this, and what I did write in my own hand stayed with the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the the investigator reinserted the text that you wrote a year before into this new statement of yours, did he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. My time is running out, I still have some seven or eight minutes left. Tell me, did you in 1997 in Serbia have to respond to accusations for unlawful possession of weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the year, but I received a suspended sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you receive a suspended sentence for the fact that you were unlawfully carrying weapons in the territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did there appear your commander Boca Medic, did he appear as a witness in your trial?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At this trial did Boca Medic state that you were a unit from the Republic of the Serbian Krajina and that you carried these weapons along because you stood guard at the oil fields in Djeletovci?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I was listening to his evidence as he gave it before the Court, but I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that he did not mention at all your membership of any unit of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at this court of law he did not make mention of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm nearing the end, I have five minutes left. Let's try and do this without documents. The Prosecution disclosed us the information that you were a witness for Sasa Cvjetan who was accused of the murder in Podujevo and the trial took place in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sasa Cvjetan, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you twice give a statement before the Belgrade court for war crimes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was once that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you in that same case before the court in Prokuplje give a statement, and then subsequently you gave a statement again when the case appeared before the court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did it turn out that you changed your testimony and that you said that at that first trial at Prokuplje you lied because you were so persuaded by the defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Kindly tell us and the Trial Chamber how did it happen that the defence counsel managed to persuade you to tell lies before a court of law to say something that was false?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The defence counsel approached a number of us and said that we ought to help and defend Cvjetan against the charges levelled at him. There were four of us who appeared in this -- at this trial, and he wrote us in brief terms on a -- wrote to us on in brief terms on a piece of paper what it was that we were supposed to state before the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just consult with my client, but I'm at the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have three more minutes which I would like to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you were shown some payment certificates for the payments you received from the MUP of Serbia, as you said. Was it your salary or per diems?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the heading said per diems.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you what it said, I am asking you how you understood the payments. Were those per diems or salaries?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please explain what the factual difference is, how you -- how you can see whether it's the one or the other. So ask the witness whether he has any factual information about that. I mean, if I get a certain amount of money, then of course you can ask yourself what it is, a per diem or a salary, but how to see the difference and on the basis of what to make such a determination, these are the factual matters that would assist the Chamber in knowing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, would you kindly tell me, since you didn't sign any contracts, as you have just told us, how come you received payments from the JSO, based on what?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was there, I was in the area, I suppose it was in good order for me to be paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mean in Tara?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Tara we were given a small allowance, just to cover our costs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But when you say that you were there in the field, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem in the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us yourself yesterday that the per diems that the Prosecutor showed to you, you started receiving them on the 16th of August, 1995. What kind of salaries could there have been before that date, before the 16th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention any payments. I didn't mention any salaries. I was in the field on the ground and every fortnight we received money.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who did you receive the money from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A commander whose name was Rasko, an active member of the JSO was the one who distributed money amongst us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did he do that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he received the money, he would distribute it amongst us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before the 18th of August, were you a member of the JSO at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Tara, I first went to the village of Njemci and then into a forest, and throughout the entire time of my engagement I was in that forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After the Tara stint, after September you were in a forest, you received -- okay. How much money did you receive? What was your salary?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you said to the investigative judge Dilparic at the hearing here, you told him that you received only two salaries from the JSO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer? I thought that I was there for two months. That's why I said two salaries, and then later on here I saw the payrolls and then I realised that it was every fortnight. So two salaries each fortnight, two payments each fortnight is one monthly salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stoparic, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, I want to make a note on the record that the documents which I acknowledged on Tuesday the Prosecution had failed to provide in advance of this witness's testimony have all been translated and provided in advance of today's hearings. Some were provided yesterday. I do not recall Mr. Jordash asking any questions referring to that material, so I just wanted to ask him to confirm that he had received the documents and the English translation of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, it's just about receipt Mr. Groome is asking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We are talking about the witness's testimony from the previous --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The documents that Mr. Bakrac has just made inquiries about, the previous testimony in Serbian courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I have been provide with, I think, two documents. It's the testimony in, I think, the Kosevan -- a court in Kosovo, it's not, though, the totality of the witness's previous testimony that we were seeking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then I'll explore with Mr. Jordash after the hearing if there's additional material which he believes that we are obliged -- it's my understanding at this stage we've turned over all of the material that we were obliged and committed ourselves to turning over. If that's not the case then --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, I think it might be right. I think it might be right that the Prosecution have given us what they have in their possession what I'm referring to as previous testimony which isn't, it seems, in the Prosecution's possession but which relates to what the witness has said before in either the court in Kosovo or more likely the Belgrade court in relation to the prosecution of Sasa, which we haven't had sight of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to keep matters clear. I remember that there was the Canadian statement or the Canadian testimony. Then we had testimony in a court in Belgrade which indicated that in an earlier -- at an earlier occasion the witness would not have told the truth. Now, those earlier testimonies or statements, have they been disclosed where apparently he would have said something not in accordance with the truth. I don't remember that you said that you had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I said that I would inquire whether we had it, and I said that we had a large file that I didn't know at the time. When we checked that large file, we found not only the witness's testimony from the Belgrade case but also the previous case, the trial case as it were, from, I don't recall the name but it began with a P and it was in Kosovo. So three items have been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have the Belgrade and the history of that. Now, I am a bit confused about The Hague statement because that seems to be a Serbian court where the investigating judge takes a statement in The Hague. I heard Mr. Bakrac referring to The Hague. Where do I have to place that? It's not Canadian, is it one of the big file or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes -- no, Your Honours, no. What has been disclosed -- yes, this was disclosed by the Prosecutor on the 7th of July, 2003. That's when the investigating judge of the Belgrade court was here in The Hague and took a statement from witness Stoparic. Just give me a moment and I'll tell you the 65 ter number. I have it right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm mainly interested to establish where the disclosure issues are. Apparently if that was disclosed at such an early stage, there's no disclosure issue in relation to that. Then Mr. Jordash, do I understand you well that you received the Canadian stuff to say so, the Belgrade and history of that material, and that you are not sure whether you've received everything, and that Mr. Groome says that's what we have?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the position. Is that your position as well, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I think we have at least clarified that. Canada plus Belgrade and the history of Belgrade, previous statements, firstly The Hague statement was there already and is not the subject of any disclosure dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, I just have a few questions for you. One of them I want to ask to you explain in a little greater detail in an answer you you gave to Mr. Jordash yesterday and is found at transcript page 10461. You said -- and he was asking you questions about your responsibilities or the responsibilities of the Skorpions in Djeletovci. "Well, you see, on one occasion Medic told me this: The border belongs to the military and the oil wells to the state security because the latter facility was of a strategic importance. That's what he meant when he said that." Can I ask you to explain the portion of that where you said that the facility, the latter facility was of strategic importance. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what he said to all of us. He said that the border belonged to the military. What he meant was that the Army of Republic of Serbian Krajina would be responsible for the border, and within that same context since we were guarding the border we would be answerable to the military. And as for the oil fields, they belonged to, or rather, did not belong to but that the state security was interested in the oil fields because the oil fields were of a strategic interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know why the oil fields were of strategic interest?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, the oil fields made a profit for the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, today at transcript page 9 in response to a question by Mr. Jordash, you indicated that during the period of time for which payment records of the state security service indicate you were paid monies, you were simply a reservist. You weren't actively working. Now, my earlier examination of you you mentioned a few other names that you recognised on those same payment lists. Those being Goran Simovic, Goran Jovic, Laza Kresovic, and Zlatoje Bozic. My question to you now is do you know whether these men were also reservists during the periods reflected in the payment records?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Objection. At the time that my learned friend asked that question of the witness and detailed these four men and had the witness confirm that he knew them, the Prosecution declined to continue that examination, and I wondered at the time what that was all about, and I intentionally chose not to open that subject during cross-examination, and I don't think counsel for Mr. Simatovic did either. In light of that approach, in our submission, the Prosecution ought not to now be allowed to open it at the last minute

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, please responds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm just looking for the exact question that -- so on page 9, Mr. Jordash says: "And you made that supposition from August onwards that you were being paid by the DB as a result of being a reservist." So it's Mr. Jordash that has put to the witness that he was a reservist on this list. I'm simply asking the witness whether the other people he recognised on this list, whether he knows them to also be reservists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But I have no way touched the subject of what status the other four had on the list. The Prosecution obviously had in mind what status those four had on a list when they examined the witness in -- during the direct examination, and they chose not to open it, and I chose not to touch it, and asking the witness about his status is in no way relevant to the other four on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you -- do you know whether the other people that you recognise were reservists? Do you want me to repeat the entire question or do you understand?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood the question. Goran Jovic, Laza Kresovic, and the last one were just like me, they were reservists. Whereas Goran Simovic, I'm not sure. I am not sure about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, during your time as a reserve member, as you put it, of the JSO, did you encounter any members who were considered active members?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander was an active officer. For awhile I was transferred to the light mobile infantry and our commander there was an active member of the JSO. His name was Rasko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any difference in the way that active members were paid and reserve members were paid?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that active members were better paid than us, although they received per diems at the same time as we did. There were some dozen active members who had their little tents close to ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could he just repeat -- could the witness repeat, I don't want to suggest. The record is wrong. The witness said that he believed that active --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not going to tell the witness what he has said. We will ask him to repeat it and to see whether you are then satisfied with the way in which his words are transcribed. Could you tell us -- well, I'll slowly read to you what is recorded as being your answer. Please correct me if in any way that is not a proper recording of what you said. Your answer is recorded as: "I believe that active members were better paid than us, although they received monies at the same time as we did. There were some dozen active members who had their little tents close to ours." That is what was recorded as your answer. Is that in any way inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bakrac, you have an opportunity to check on the original B/C/S tape and ask for a rectification of translation and/or transcript, but we can't listen back to what the witness says at this very moment, but of course you have an opportunity to challenge the accuracy of the transcript and the translation in this respect. You know how to do it. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, did either the active members or the reserve members receive a receipt or any paperwork when they received their payment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were identical lists or payrolls identical to the ones that you showed me. I located my name on the payroll and I signed next to the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, the Chamber considers that at this moment you are really seeking the boundaries of what we allowed you to do under the earlier objection of Mr. Jordash. So you could have asked the witness, you have asked him many questions about payments, you could have asked him on receipts at that moment if you had wished to do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That was the last question I intended, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At transcript page 36 today, you were ask about Pauk and whether you knew a person by the name of Mile Novakovic. Did you ever see an order signed by Mile Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you ever -- do you recall ever hearing Mr. Medic saying that he had been given an order by Mile Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you, Mr. Witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that I think you said on the 11th of July you were not yet a member of the reserve unit but that you rather were with the Skorpions. Where were you exactly on that date you mentioned with the Skorpions? And I think as a matter of fact that we were talking about the 11th of June. I'll read to you what your answer was. It was the document where there was some dispute about whether it states June or August, and you said: "I wasn't on the reserve force of the MUP of Serbia on the 11th of June, rather I was in the Skorpions." Where were you with the Skorpions at that moment in time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My last field mission with the Skorpions was in Trnovo, so we were supposed to be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You've also told us that when you were with the Skorpions, you also received a salary or at least money from Serbia. You told us about three sources, the oil industry, directly from your commander, and money from Serbia. Did you receive money from Serbia when you, as you said, on the 11th of June you were in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we all received salaries in the same way. However, while on field missions we did not receive salaries. We received the monies due to us when we returned to our base in Djeletovci. They would then pay us all of the arrears that had accrued while we were on field missions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, was there any time between the moment that you left the Skorpions and when you were engaged by the reserve unit where you were, so to say, unemployed by either, so you were not employed by Skorpions nor by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a period. I can't tell you how long the period was, but I was at home for a week or perhaps two. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my next question is, you joined the MUP unit, as you said, in August. Could you tell us exactly when you left that unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: October, November. I don't know. It was already cold. I can't remember. Judging by the certificate that I showed you that was here, it should have been the 22nd but I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember how you you received that document? Did you ask for it, or?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask for it. We arrived at Pajzos, there were some depots there, that's where we returned our equipment, bagfuls of weapons, and when that was done a bus was waiting for us to return us to Sid, and since I was from Sid that was brilliant because I didn't have to go anywhere else. A civilian came, a man in civilian clothes came, he called our names and he issued the certificates to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that certificate is dated the 12th of December. Were you at any moment after the 12th of December still engaged by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosovo. Many years later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, the document says that you were engaged until the 22nd of December. How can you write down on the 12th that you are engaged up to a date which has not yet passed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assure you that when I received the certificate, I was at home that very same day. Now, why the difference, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. I have no further questions. Have the questions of the Bench or the questions by Mr. Groome triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then before we'll excuse the witness, Mr. Jordash, at this point in time we started the testimony of the witness with quite some disclosure issues. Is there anything to be added at this moment to it, or are you still considering whether or not there would ever be a necessity to recall the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We are still considering it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are still considering that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It looks less likely than it did at the beginning of the examination, but we haven't come to a final decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Same question for Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to see it if the Prosecution has it. I trust Mr. Groome fully when he says that he didn't know of this piece of paper, but nevertheless it would be good if the Prosecution could look into that and try and see if they have that piece of paper and based on that we would judge if there would eventually be any need for it. That would be my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just to be clear on what we are speaking about, is this the -- when the witness referred to a handwritten note that he presented to the Prosecutor? Is that the note that we are speaking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we are talking about the handwritten note the witness prepared the evening before he was interviewed and in which he laid down what caused him to join and what his opinion was about the political developments also referring to Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will investigate that matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will investigate that. Mr. Jordash, when could we hear whether what now is said to be less likely, when will you have made up your mind? Because I'm going to instruct the witness not to speak with anyone about his testimony, but of course, we wouldn't impose silence upon him forever.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: One month. Would that be acceptable to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, may I take it that within this one month, you, Mr. Groome, would also have been able to see whether there's any such handwritten note?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. And I would like to instruct you that you still should not speak about your testimony with anyone, whether parties or friends or family. Not to speak and also not to communicate in any other way because there is a chance, although perhaps a small chance, that when the parties have further studied some materials that you would be recalled. Therefore, you are not yet finally excused as a witness. Nevertheless, the Chamber hopes that within approximately a month from now, we can send you a message whether my instruction still stands or whether you are finally excused as a witness, which means that you are free to talk and communicate with whomever you want, of course, within the limits of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Is this clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to invite you to follow the Usher and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, there's one thing that comes to my mind and that is that I think I invited you the day before yesterday to make submissions on a postponement in writing. We have not received anything yet, I don't know whether -- when we'll receive that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's almost complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's almost complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It can be filed early tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Early tomorrow morning. Mr. Groome, it seems to me that this is not a matter which should remain undecided, in whatever way we'll decide the matter, too long. Therefore I'm asking you how much time you will need to respond even though I am I aware that you have not yet seen the application, but you know more or less what Mr. Jordash wants to raise because he started already to explain why he wanted a postponement of the proceedings after the recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that for next Wednesday? I'm already losing staff to the holiday break, if -- I'm not sure who is here to look at it. I would ask Mr. Jordash to please send courtesy copies so we can get working on it as soon as possible, but there are a number of other projects that I have the limited staff I have working on which are equally important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when do you think we could receive courtesy copies of your response?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm saying Wednesday, is that acceptable for the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's for the courtesy. Yes. Of course, the Judges, if we would have an opportunity to even look at what both parties have submitted before Christmas, that would be preferable because next week Friday and the week after that on Monday are UN holidays, and therefore we might be -- not be able to communicate as we usually do. Therefore, if there would be by any chance if it would be possible for you to already finish it by Tuesday, close of business, that would be highly appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And we'll make every attempt to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any other matters at this moment to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There's one last issue from the Stanisic Defence. Your Honour set a dead-line today for the Defence to inform the Chamber concerning JF-004 and whether we might want to cross-examine him further. This, I'm pausing just in case I say anything that I ought not to in public, but it's concerning the intercepts and we were instructed or we indicated we wanted to speak to a expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We haven't managed to find one as yet and the situation is that we are still looking and expect the search to take a while longer. And we would ask the Trial Chamber to keep open the cross-examination of this witness a while longer also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, in view of the explanation given by Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no objection. I have no objection to whatever time is needed, I just wonder, some of these dead-lines that Mr. Jordash is requesting seem that they are pushing very close to the time that I anticipate that I will be resting the Prosecution case and that would be an impediment to my being able to do that, if there were still witnesses outstanding to be able to be cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we first allow you to -- if we would change the dead-line to the 15th of January to start with but then really expect an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I cannot see how the situation would be any different given the Christmas break. I can inform the Chamber what we are doing. We initially were looking at an expert within Serbia. That's not proven possible, and we are now looking internationally to see if we can find and expert and that brings with it obvious problems, and we are doing what we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, the 15th of January is set as date in which you either have met the matter covered by the dead-line as we had it or to further explain why you need more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then of course we are asking for detailed information.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On a somewhat related matter, there's a witness, JF -- I believe it's 59, I'm just trying to call up my records here, but it's the witness that the Simatovic Defence had said that they were unable to cross-examine. We will be scheduling these people in during the break. I don't know if there's -- there's no pending application that I am aware of. If Mr. Bakrac knows that there will be none, that would assist the Prosecution in making its final arrangements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's precisely what I wanted to request. As soon as we break for today, I will go through this witness's statement and everything else that we couldn't do, and if I could have the 10th of January as a dead-line for my response to the Prosecution, if there's any need to call him and to provide a reasoning or an explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, 10th of January is an offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll leave it to the Chamber on that. I just want to correct the record, it's JF-052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do you oppose against the 10th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He is -- the witness we now have scheduled to -- is 19th of January, so it's not an awful lot of time for a response and decision by the Court and to set up a video conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so if we would make it --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll do my best. I'll try and do it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, we'll go just in between the two Christmases. Still this year you are supposed to respond, then you are still heading for Christmas, Mr. Groome has had his Christmas already, I take it, and then can further prepare. This brings me to my --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the final thing I'd like to say is that we'll adjourn. As scheduled at this moment, we'll resume on the 10th of January but, of course, all dependant on a decision on a motion which we have not yet received. Whatever we will do in January, I first of all want to wish -- give my best wishes for everyone for the Christmas Day, for the new year. Although I am aware that not everyone in this courtroom is -- will be able to be at home at his Christmas, I nevertheless hope that Christmas and the new year will bring everyone what he expects from it. We stand adjourned.
